3. If the sensor would reliably detect the required signal, no detection challenges that requirement.

activity.prompt: A model requires a signal of at least 3 units. A reliable sensor detects 1 unit or more, yet an independently verified event gives no detection. What follows?
choices: Any positive signal must have been exactly 3 units
activity.explanation: A signal meeting the 3-unit requirement would exceed the 1-unit threshold. The event therefore challenges that requirement, while not proving an untested alternative.

evidence.title: A new required signal
evidence.context: An event is confirmed independently. Other model conditions hold; the sensor is reliable.

evidence.title: Testing a vapor requirement
evidence.context: An event is confirmed. The model requires at least 12 mg/L vapor; all other conditions hold.

tip: Compare the prediction with the sensor limit before interpreting “not detected.”

title: Explain opposite seasons
body: 1. Earth’s rotation gives day and night. Its orbit gives the yearly cycle.
2. The axis keeps the same tilt direction as Earth orbits. Each hemisphere takes a turn leaning toward the Sun.
3. A shared Earth–Sun distance cannot by itself explain longer days in one hemisphere and shorter days in the other.

activity.prompt: Matched northern and southern latitudes have opposite changes in daylight over six months. Which mechanism explains the contrast?
choices: The changing orientation of Earth’s tilted axis toward the Sun
A shared Earth–Sun distance change by itself
The changing illuminated fraction of the Moon
activity.explanation: Axial tilt changes each hemisphere’s illumination geometry over the orbit. A shared distance change alone does not explain opposite hemisphere day lengths, and lunar phase does not produce the seasonal pattern.

evidence.title: Another pair of latitudes
evidence.context: Each site keeps its latitude. Earth rotates throughout both observations.

evidence.title: Daylight at matched latitudes
evidence.context: Northern and southern sites are equally far from the equator. Values are illustrative.

tip: Opposite daylight changes point to tilt, not a distance change shared by Earth.

title: Put rock events in order
body: 1. In undisturbed upright layers, lower layers formed first.
2. A feature cutting a rock formed after that rock. An unbroken layer deposited over a fault formed after that fault movement.
3. Join these clues into one sequence. They give order, not exact ages.

activity.prompt: An intrusion cuts Layer M but is itself cut by Fault F. What is the order?
activity.explanation: The intrusion is later than M because it cuts M. F is later than the intrusion because it cuts the intrusion. Combine those relations as M → intrusion → F.

evidence.title: A different rock sequence
evidence.context: The observed relationships are preserved; no overturning occurred.

rows: Cuts M; cut by Fault F

evidence.title: Layers and a fault
evidence.context: The layers have not been overturned.

tip: An event cannot cut a rock that has not formed yet.

workedCases.label: Another case: a layer seals an old fault
workedCases.text:
Question: What is the order from oldest to youngest?

1. A is below B, so A formed first. The fault cuts both, so that movement came later.
2. C covers the fault without being cut, so C came after that movement.

Supported answer: A → B → fault movement → C.

Watch for: The fault is younger than the rocks it cuts, but older than the unbroken rock that covers it.

evidence.title: An unbroken top layer
evidence.context: The layers are upright and have not been overturned.

rows: Cuts A and B; ends below C

title: Name what actually happened
body: 1. Breaks down in place = weathering. Moves = erosion. Settles = deposition.
2. Liquid to vapor = evaporation. Vapor to liquid drops = condensation.
3. Name each event separately before combining a sequence.

activity.prompt: Water vapor becomes droplets on a cool pane while a nearby stream moves loose sand. Which pair names the events?
activity.explanation: Vapor-to-liquid droplets are condensation. Sand in transport is erosion; settling would be deposition and in-place breakdown would be weathering.

evidence.title: Two new observations
evidence.context: The sand remains in motion, and pane droplets form from water vapor.

evidence.title: Rock after rain
evidence.context: Follow what happens to the same material.

tip: Ask whether the material breaks, moves, settles, or changes state before naming the process.

title: Keep protons, neutrons, and electrons separate
body: 1. Protons identify the element.
2. Different neutron counts make isotopes of that same element.
3. Charge = protons − electrons. Extra electrons make a negative ion; lost electrons make a positive ion.

activity.prompt: An atom with 8 protons loses 2 of its 8 electrons without nuclear change. What results?
choices: A 2+ ion of the same element
A neutral isotope with 2 fewer neutrons
activity.explanation: Eight protons remain, so the element stays the same. Eight positive charges minus six negative charges gives +2. No neutron change is stated.

evidence.title: Losing electrons
evidence.context: Only 2 electrons are lost. The nucleus and neutron count stay unchanged.

evidence.title: Two particles
evidence.context: Particle counts refer to individual atoms or ions.

tip: Protons name the element; subtract electrons from protons to find charge.

title: Solve the reciprocal, then flip it
body: 1. In 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, first isolate 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
2. Use a common denominator to subtract. Then flip the result to recover v.
3. If 1/v = 0, there is no finite v. Do not read it as v = 0.

activity.prompt: For 1/f = 1/u + 1/v with f = 8 cm and u = 24 cm, what is v?
activity.explanation: 1/v = 1/8−1/24 = 2/24 = 1/12, so v = 12 cm. Subtract reciprocals rather than distances, then invert.

evidence.title: Another lens
evidence.context: Use 1/f = 1/u + 1/v. All distances are in cm; a finite real image forms.

evidence.title: A lens model
evidence.context: Use 1/f = 1/u + 1/v. All distances are in cm and the model applies.

tip: Write “1/v” beside the fraction until you invert it to get the distance.
